chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Muawiya or someone else, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the substance of al-usrub (a type of silver coin), and when it was pure it contained silver. Is it permissible for a man to pay an advance sum of named dirhams for it? He said: If the dominant name upon it is al-usrub, then there is no problem with that, meaning it is not recognized except by the name al-usrub.

key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمَ: Dirhams, silver coins used as currency
key_terms.الْأُسْرُبِّ: Usrub, a specific type of silver coin used in the context of the narration
key_terms.الْمُسَمَّاةَ: Named or specified (referring to the agreed amount or type of dirhams)
key_terms.جَوْهَر: Substance or core material of a coin

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging silver coins that are not pure silver in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the criteria for valid currency exchange (bay' al-darham bi al-darham) by prioritizing customary recognition ('urf') over strict chemical composition. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that as long as the coin is predominantly identified by its traditional name despite containing impurities, it retains its status for transactional purposes, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that social convention often dictates legal validity in commercial matters.
